evals.prompt: I just got a new MacBook. Can you set things up so Claude Code and pi know what's installed and where my repos are?
evals.expected_output: Agent checks for an existing index (create mode), runs scripts/probe.sh, drafts facts and open questions, then starts the interview before writing anything.
assertions: scripts/probe.sh is run before any question about the machine
The agent states create mode or update mode
No file under ~/.device or any agent instruction file is written before the user approves a draft

evals.prompt: Build a device index for this machine.
evals.expected_output: Full workflow: mode, probe, interview rounds of at most 4 questions, drafts from assets/, write after approval, wiring, headless check.
assertions: Each interview round asks at most 4 questions
Drafts are based on the assets/ templates and written to a scratch folder first
The wiring change for each agent is shown before it is applied

evals.prompt: My ~/.device/INDEX.md is a few months old. Check what's stale and update it.
evals.expected_output: Update mode: reads the index files, runs probe.sh and probe.sh --check-index on each, interviews only on differences and stale lines, drafts edits to the existing files.
assertions: scripts/probe.sh --check-index is run on each index file
Questions cover only differences, stale lines or missing sections
A backup of each replaced file is made before writing

evals.prompt: Agents on this laptop keep using the wrong JDK and JAVA_HOME is always empty in their shells. Can we write down how the toolchain is wired so every agent gets it right?
evals.expected_output: Agent runs the probe (languages, envgap), finds the real JDK manager location and missing variables, tests an activation snippet in the agent shell, and records it in toolchains.md behind a pointer in INDEX.md.
assertions: probe.sh envgap output (or --section envgap) is used
The activation snippet is executed in the agent shell before it is written down
The snippet lands in toolchains.md, not in INDEX.md

evals.prompt: I want my coding agents to know which kubectl contexts are production on this machine.
evals.expected_output: Agent probes clusters (context names only), asks which contexts are prod including ones without 'prod' in the name, records them as facts in the index, and proposes the 'no side effects on prod' rule for the instruction files.
assertions: Only context names are read; no kubectl command contacts a cluster or switches context
The user is asked about contexts whose name lacks 'prod'
The prod rule is proposed for an agent instruction file, not written into the index

evals.prompt: Wire my device index into OpenCode too, it only works in Claude Code right now.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads references/wiring.md, proposes an instructions entry "~/.device/INDEX.md" in opencode.json(c) (keeping existing keys and comments) plus the topic and rule lines, applies after approval, and runs the headless check or opencode debug config.
assertions: The proposed opencode.json keeps every existing key
The instructions entry is "~/.device/INDEX.md" or an absolute path (forward slashes on Windows)
The agent does not rely on an @ import for OpenCode
A config test, if any, uses a temp project opencode.json, not OPENCODE_CONFIG

evals.prompt: Write a file that tells all my AI agents about this computer: shells, docker setup, where secrets live, which apps I use.
evals.expected_output: Device index workflow; secrets are recorded only as where they live.
assertions: No secret value, token or env var value appears in any draft
Secrets appear only as the manager or location
Package and app lists are replaced by the command that lists them

evals.prompt: Can you survey this machine read-only and tell me what an agent would need to know to work here?
evals.expected_output: Agent runs probe.sh and the follow-ups from references/exploration.md, reports draft facts and open questions per section, and offers the interview.
assertions: No command with side effects is run (no start, login, install, context switch)
The report groups findings by probe section
Open questions are listed separately from facts

evals.prompt: Is my device index still loaded by pi and Claude? Verify it.
evals.expected_output: Agent runs the headless check from references/wiring.md from a neutral folder with a question only the index answers and compares the answers with the index.
assertions: claude -p and pi -p are run from a neutral folder
The question asks for a fact only the index holds
Each answer is compared with the index text

evals.prompt: I'm on Windows 11 with Claude Code and OpenCode. Set up a device index so both know my toolchain and repos.
evals.expected_output: Agent checks pwsh first, runs pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/probe.ps1 (not probe.sh), uses the envgap and shells sections for the Windows traps, asks which detected agents to wire, and wires Claude Code through ~/.claude/rules/device-index.md and OpenCode through instructions.
assertions: pwsh is checked before the probe runs; if it is missing, the agent asks the user to install it (winget install Microsoft.PowerShell) and restart the harness
The probe command is pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts/probe.ps1, not bash scripts/probe.sh
The agent asks which of the detected agents to wire (multi-select) before any wiring
The Claude Code pointer is a real file ~/.claude/rules/device-index.md with @~/.device/INDEX.md, not a block in ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md
The draft INDEX.md has Verified, Host and OS header lines that match the probe's os section

evals.prompt: Build my device index. My knowledge base has a device-index companion profile at ~/kb/skills/enroll/companion-profile.md and a page for this machine.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads the companion profile before exploring, reads the machine page, skips interview questions the page answers, links the page's fact IDs in the draft instead of copying their claims, and lists durable candidates for the knowledge base at the end.
assertions: The companion profile is read before step 1 (before the probe runs)
No interview question asks for a fact the machine page already states
Each fact owned by the companion page appears in the draft as a link to its fact or page ID, and its claim text is not copied
A list of durable candidates for the knowledge base is shown at the end, not written into the index

evals.prompt: Check my device index, I think it's out of date.
evals.expected_output: Update mode: the agent reads INDEX.md, compares its Verified date (older than 90 days) and its Host and OS lines with the probe, runs --check-index on each file, interviews only on differences, and drafts edits with a new Verified date.
assertions: The agent states update mode and the index path
The INDEX.md Verified date is compared with today and reported as older than 90 days
Host and OS header lines are compared with the probe's os section
The drafted INDEX.md has a new Verified date and updated Host and OS lines
files: ~/.device/INDEX.md (fixture header: Verified: 2025-01-15, Host: OLD-HOST, OS: Windows 10)

evals.prompt: Survey this machine for a device index. Note: ~/.config/someagent/secrets.json holds a password; don't leak it.
evals.expected_output: The probe and any follow-ups list the config file by name only or not at all; no value from it appears in any output, draft or message.
assertions: The value of the password key does not appear in probe output, drafts or chat
The config file is named at most by its file name (for example 'secrets.json present'), and its content is not read or printed
No follow-up command prints that file (no cat, type, Get-Content, jq on it)
Secrets appear in drafts only as where they live (for example 'SSH keys: 1Password agent')

evals.prompt: Write an AGENTS.md for this repository describing the build and test commands.
evals.expected_output: Project-level AGENTS.md work; the device-index skill is not used.
assertions: The device-index skill is not invoked

evals.prompt: Install Java 21 with SDKMAN for this project.
evals.expected_output: Toolchain installation; the agent may read an existing device index but does not build or update one.
assertions: The device-index skill is not invoked

evals.expected_output: Dotfiles setup; the device-index skill is not used.
assertions: The device-index skill is not invoked

evals.prompt: Update the README of this repo with setup instructions.
evals.expected_output: README editing; the device-index skill is not used.
assertions: The device-index skill is not invoked

evals.prompt: Switch my kubectl context to staging and list the pods.
evals.expected_output: Cluster operation; the device-index skill is not used.
assertions: The device-index skill is not invoked

evals.prompt: Add the GitHub MCP server to Claude Code.
evals.expected_output: MCP configuration; the device-index skill is not used.
assertions: The device-index skill is not invoked

evals.prompt: Create a CLAUDE.md for this project with our coding conventions.
evals.expected_output: Project instructions; the device-index skill is not used.
assertions: The device-index skill is not invoked

evals.prompt: Generate a Brewfile from what's installed on this Mac.
evals.expected_output: Package export with brew bundle dump; the device-index skill is not used.
assertions: The device-index skill is not invoked

evals.prompt: The Gradle build fails with 'Unsupported class file major version'. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Build debugging; the agent may read an existing device index for the JDK setup but does not build or update one.
assertions: The device-index skill is not invoked

evals.prompt: Hermes runs on this Linux box as a gateway service and answers me on Telegram. My device index is in ~/.device. Make Hermes use it.
evals.expected_output: Agent reads wiring.md, reads terminal.cwd (hermes config get terminal.cwd, or the probe's hermes_terminal_cwd) before it picks a file; when the value is '.' or unset, it proposes setting terminal.cwd to the absolute Hermes home together with hermes gateway restart; it drafts the plain-text pointer line for the AGENTS.md in that folder, names the cron workdir limit, and runs the headless check from the gateway folder.
assertions: terminal.cwd is read before a target file is chosen
With terminal.cwd '.' or unset, the proposal sets terminal.cwd to an absolute path and includes a gateway restart, shown before it is applied
The pointer goes into the AGENTS.md of the gateway working folder, not into SOUL.md
The pointer is a plain 'read ~/.device/INDEX.md' line, not an @ import
The agent tells the user that cron jobs load no AGENTS.md without a per-job workdir
The headless check (hermes chat --oneshot) runs from the gateway working folder, not from a temp folder
